Timeout

I clicked save and it spins forever, then says the request timed out. Is it the network or the server?

The maximum time to wait for a result before giving up and reporting failure·When a save action ends in 'Request timed out', the page has reached a wait limit; this does not prove the request failed to arrive or the server crashed. Check whether the timeout happened during connection, sending, or waiting for the response, then distinguish it from rate limiting or invalid input.

In this example the request reached the service; the page reports a timeout first, while the service may continue and write later.

This timeline assumes the request reached the service; other timeouts may happen during connection or sending. Identify the timed-out stage before choosing a limit.

What happens when a timeout fires

The waiting side gives up: When a wait phase exceeds its limit, the page or tool stops waiting and reports a timeout. If the request reached the service, work may continue there; a connection or send timeout can happen before the service receives the request.

A timeout is not an error verdict: A slow response, a busy server, or large data can all exceed the limit. The failure signal only says no result arrived; the cause still needs timing and logs.

Different from rate limiting: Rate limiting rejects too many requests per period and returns 429 quickly. A timeout means waiting a long time with no response. They need different handling.

What it does not fix

Setting a very long timeout does not solve the problem: the page spins and users think it is stuck. First check whether the connection, send, or response wait timed out; then choose the limit and retry rule. Duplicate submissions can apply an action more than once.

“

The save API sometimes takes over 10 seconds, the page reports a timeout, but the data is actually written. Find which step is slow, set a reasonable wait limit and retry rule for this request, and prevent duplicate submissions while it is still processing.
